dublinCore.title: Microphone Frequency Visualization with FFT
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal processing
FFT
Audio analysis
Frequency spectrum
Data visualization
dublinCore.description: A real-time spectrum analyzer for the microphone: a 512-bin FFT of live sound drawn as color-coded frequency bars on a decibel scale, with a peak-frequency read-out, a Start/Stop control that freezes the last spectrum, and a slider that sets the highest frequency shown.
relation: Chapter 7: DFT, FFT and Frequency Domain Analysis

learningObjectives: Identify the dominant frequency of a whistled or hummed sound using the Peak read-out and the gold marker
Calculate the center frequency of an FFT bin from its index, the sample rate and the number of bins, and use it to explain why the read-out differs from the true frequency of a tone
Compare the spectra of a hummed note, a whistle and a hissed sss by the number, spacing and spread of their peaks
Predict how the Max Freq slider rescales the frequency axis, and explain why the axis cannot extend past the Nyquist frequency
Interpret the decibel scale of the vertical axis, including the 6 dB rise that comes from doubling a tone's amplitude
prerequisites: What a spectrum is and what the DFT computes

misconceptions.misconception: The Peak read-out is the exact pitch of the sound
misconceptions.correction: The FFT measures energy in bins fs/(2*512) wide (46.875 Hz at 48 kHz); the read-out reports the center of the strongest bin
misconceptions.evidence: Play a 440 Hz tone: at a 48 kHz sample rate the read-out shows 422 Hz (bin 9)

misconceptions.misconception: A voice is a single frequency
misconceptions.correction: A hummed or sung note is a fundamental plus harmonics at whole-number multiples of it
misconceptions.evidence: Hum a steady note with Max Freq at 2 kHz and press Stop: the frozen spectrum shows evenly spaced peaks

accessibility.screenReaderScript: FFT Microphone Visualizer. Press Start and allow microphone access to see the live frequency spectrum of the sound around you as colored bars, from blue at low frequencies to red at high frequencies, with the strongest frequency shown in hertz. The slider sets the highest frequency displayed.

controls.label: Start / Stop
controls.description: Start opens the microphone and begins the analysis; Stop releases the microphone and freezes the last spectrum

controls.label: Max Freq
controls.description: Sets the highest frequency on the horizontal axis; values above the Nyquist frequency fs/2 are limited to fs/2

visualElements.description: Bar chart of the 512-bin FFT magnitude in decibels (-100 to -30 dB) versus frequency, colored blue to red across the displayed range
Status line (Listening / Stopped) and the Peak read-out with a gold marker on the strongest bin

model.description: A 512-bin FFT of the live microphone signal (Web Audio AnalyserNode via p5.sound), displayed in decibels
algorithms: Peak search that skips the DC bin and its leakage

instructionalStrategies: Predict the spectrum of a sound, then make the sound and check
Freeze a spectrum with Stop and measure harmonic spacing
extensions: Interpolate the peak between bins to estimate pitch more precisely
